title: Milan: ITB test run + graded eccentric block
terrain: flat road or treadmill, zero descent

steps.note: ITB CHECK STOP: palpate, 5 slow single-leg bends, compare against minute 10

coachNotes: MONDAY READ, 24 AUG: band tender to press and to stretch, silent in normal movement. That is not ITBS, that is tissue sensitivity 48h after roughly 1990m of descent, and it is the expected result rather than a warning. The 5 September single-climb contingency does NOT fire on this. Systemic markers are green and are not the limiter: HRV 68 against a 60-day mean of 60, 7/60 ratio 1.05, resting HR 49, ATL down from 79.9 to 60.0 in two days. TEST IT PROPERLY BEFORE YOU RUN, SIXTY SECONDS. Noble compression: sit with the knee bent, find the bony bump on the outside of the knee about 2-3cm above the joint line, press firmly with your thumb and hold the pressure, then slowly straighten and re-bend the knee through that position five times. Sharp, familiar, reproducible pain arriving right there as the knee passes about 30 degrees is a positive test. Vague tenderness under static pressure that does not spike at 30 degrees is a negative test, and is what you almost certainly have. This distinction is the whole point, because 'hurts when I press it' and 'positive Noble' are indistinguishable from the outside and they mean completely different things. Then five slow single-leg squats to 30 degrees per side in front of a mirror: pain plus the opposite hip dropping is the combination that matters. THE RUN IS THE REAL TEST, AND THE TELL IS DIRECTION OF TRAVEL. ITBS gets worse the longer you run and does not warm up. Post-descent soreness fades inside the first ten minutes. That is why there is a check stop at minute 30 in the steps: stop, palpate, five slow single-leg bends, and compare against how it felt at minute 10. Worse than minute 10 means walk home and Thursday's incline session comes off. Same or better means finish the run and the gym goes ahead. ECCENTRIC BLOCK, GRADED TODAY rather than gated all-or-nothing. Step-downs are the single most ITB-provocative thing in the gym because they load precisely the 20-30 degree flexion band, so earn them set by set: set 1 is 10 reps per leg from a LOW box, 20cm, four-second lowering, then reassess. Clean means sets 2 and 3 at 25-30cm as originally prescribed. Any lateral knee pain during set 1 means step-downs are finished for the day, no negotiation, and you go straight to the rest. Nordic curls 3x5 with a slow lower, split squats 3x8 per leg with 4s down, side-lying hip abduction 3x15, Copenhagen planks 3x20s per side, single-leg calf raises 3x12. Those five carry no ITB risk and go ahead whatever the step-downs do. The lowering phase is the whole point. FULL GYM AVAILABLE IN MILAN, so no substitutions needed. Milan Tue-Thu is the only gym window you have, the NL coast has none, so this does not get postponed to the weekend. ALONE UNTIL FRIDAY EVENING. Seven hours of sleep is worth more than any session below and you are averaging 6.5h over the last week; this is the only stretch in the next three weeks where fixing that is purely a decision. HOMEWORK TONIGHT: check whether your gels and drink mix are glucose or maltodextrin only, or a glucose-fructose blend. Single-transporter products cap absorption around 60 g/h whatever the gut training does; blends clear that ceiling. It is the one input that could raise the race intake target above 60 g/h and it needs answering this week, not on 5 September.
